sentence: Ayşe’nin dün yazdığı mektubu Mehmet bugün okudu.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses head-final X-bar structures and the traditional GB placement of external arguments in Spec-IP. Ayşe’nin is the genitive subject of the nominalized relative clause, not a possessor of the external noun. Dün adjoins to the relative VP and modifies the writing event. Yazdığı takes a silent NP operator as its object; this position will become the relative-clause gap. In the separate matrix IP, Mehmet is the subject, mektubu is the object of okudu, and bugün adjoins to the matrix VP. The matrix clause therefore starts in subject–object–verb order; the sentence-initial object will be derived by scrambling. The lexical words are entered already inflected: yazdığı contains the nominalizing participial morphology and third-person singular agreement, while mektubu contains accusative morphology. Their internal morphemes are not represented as separate terminals. Abstract I heads represent the corresponding inflectional features. Both verbs assign Agent and Theme roles. Matrix I licenses nominative on Mehmet, and each verb governs and licenses accusative on its object; the relative operator's case is abstract and unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative-clause and matrix-clause base structures.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Yazdığı raises from the V position shown in the preceding workspace and adjoins to the relative I head. Its original position becomes an unpronounced verbal trace. This lexicalist GB analysis moves the already-inflected word rather than deriving its spelling by combining separately represented morphemes. The resulting I complex checks the participial and agreement features. Nominalized I licenses genitive on Ayşe’nin, and Spec-head agreement connects that subject to the third-person singular agreement of yazdığı. The operator remains in the object position: its subsequent A-bar movement has not yet occurred. The separate matrix IP is unchanged because relative-clause formation is still being completed.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb to nominalized I and license its genitive subject.

values.licensing: local government by the verbal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative C projects a head-final CP over the nominalized IP. The null operator moves from the previously established object position to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace. The operator A-bar binds that trace, producing the open relative predicate ‘the entity that Ayşe wrote yesterday’. The Theme role and abstract object Case belong to the chain through its base position. The object trace remains locally governed by the verbal trace, which belongs to the V-to-I chain. Neither the operator nor C is pronounced. The matrix clause remains separate until this relative CP can be attached to its nominal head.
derivationStages.statement: Form the relative CP by moving the null object operator.

values.interpretation: restrictive modification of the letter as the Theme of Ayşe's writing

derivationStages.stageRecord: The completed CP adjoins on the left of the object's N′, giving the prenominal restrictive relative Ayşe’nin dün yazdığı. Its operator variable is identified with the external nominal head mektubu. The external noun is not moved out of the relative clause: this is a head-external operator analysis. Its accusative Case comes from the matrix verb, independently of the relative object's abstract Case. After attachment, okudu raises from its previously shown V position to matrix I and leaves a verbal trace. The resulting inflectional head agrees with Mehmet and retains past tense. The entire modified object is still in the matrix verb's complement position, so this workspace explicitly supplies the source for the later object scrambling.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the relative clause to the object noun and raise the matrix verb.

values.licensing: local government by the verbal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: The entire accusative NP moves from the matrix complement position established in the preceding stage to a left-adjoined position on IP. The relative clause travels with its nominal head; no extraction from the relative clause occurs. An unpronounced NP trace remains as the matrix verb's complement. This analysis treats the clause-peripheral scrambling as an A-bar dependency, with the lower position preserving the object's Theme role and accusative licensing. Mehmet remains in Spec-IP, and bugün remains a matrix VP adjunct. The resulting pronounced order is exactly Ayşe’nin dün yazdığı mektubu Mehmet bugün okudu. The sentence means that Mehmet read today the letter that Ayşe wrote yesterday. The two temporal adverbs modify their respective writing and reading events; the structure does not impose a separate contrastive or topical discourse interpretation on the fronted object.
derivationStages.statement: Scramble the complete object NP to the left edge and complete the sentence.
